title: Fathering Fundamentals

welcome.title: Ken and Micah
welcome.ken: These are the Seven Secrets I have taught fathers for decades. Short sessions you can use the same night. Not a theory class. A way to be the man your child can count on.
welcome.micah: I built this path so you can start tonight. Each session is short. Watch, take the questions if they are there, try one move at home. I will walk it with you. Here's session one.

subtitle: The Seven Secrets of Effective Fathers Assessment & Course
note: Migrated from older 5-session Keystone pack to live Seven Secrets structure (Intro + 7). Ken film URLs pending; shape stills are placeholders.

sessions.title: Introduction

checkpoint.prompt: What should you do before the First Secret sessions?
choices: Skip the assessment and jump to Session 1
Watch the overview and take the free assessment
Wait until you finish all seven secrets

checkpoint.prompt: What is this course built on?
choices: Dr. Ken Canfield's research-based Seven Secrets

checkpoint.prompt: Why take the assessment first?
choices: So growth targets are personal, not generic
So you can skip hard sessions
So the course can grade your child

sessions.keyline: Welcome, overview, and take the assessment.
sessions.practice: Complete the free assessment before Session 1.

sessions.title: First Secret: Commitment

checkpoint.prompt: What does the First Secret treat as essential?
choices: Being present physically, emotionally, and spiritually

checkpoint.prompt: What does commitment build, per this session?
Which practice matches this session?
choices: Name one physical, one emotional, and one spiritual way you will show up this week

sessions.keyline: Present physically, emotionally, spiritually; commitment builds trust.
sessions.practice: Name one physical, one emotional, and one spiritual way you will show up this week.

sessions.title: Second Secret: Knowing Your Child

checkpoint.prompt: What opens deeper connection in the Second Secret?
choices: Knowing your child's unique personality, needs, and interests

checkpoint.prompt: Knowing your child means mainly:
choices: Entering their world so they feel seen

checkpoint.prompt: A practical move for this secret is to:
choices: Write a current profile of the child, with the mother or caregiver if that channel is safe

sessions.keyline: Unique personality, needs, and interests open deeper connection.
sessions.practice: Write a one-page profile of who this child is now (personality, fears, current passions, next six months), with the mother or caregiver if that channel is safe. No visit required.

sessions.title: Third Secret: Showing Up Consistently

checkpoint.prompt: What does Showing Up Consistently create?
choices: Stability through consistent actions, values, and discipline

checkpoint.prompt: Consistency here is mainly about:
choices: Keeping a rhythm your child can count on

checkpoint.prompt: If you must miss a standing time, the strong move is:
choices: Write the new time down, and keep it
Make it up with a gift only

sessions.keyline: Stability through consistent actions, values, and discipline.
sessions.practice: Pick one action, one value, and one discipline habit you will keep the same this week.

sessions.title: Fourth Secret: Protecting and Providing Security

checkpoint.prompt: Protecting and Providing Security covers:
choices: Physical, emotional, and spiritual safety and provision

checkpoint.prompt: Security for a child often feels like:
choices: A father who keeps them safe and provided for across those dimensions

checkpoint.prompt: A practical focus this week is:
choices: Name one way you will protect or provide security this week

sessions.keyline: Physical, emotional, and spiritual safety and provision.
sessions.practice: Name one protective move and one provision move you will make this week.

sessions.title: Fifth Secret: Loving Their Mother

checkpoint.prompt: This secret still applies when you are not a couple. What does it require?
choices: Honor her in how you speak. Never undercut her.
Pretend you are a couple again.

checkpoint.prompt: Why does this secret exist?
choices: Children should not have to choose a side or hear you tear her down.

checkpoint.prompt: Which practice matches this session?
choices: One sentence you will not say, and one civil child-only note if the channel is safe
Ask the child to carry a message to her

sessions.keyline: Honor their mother. Civil if you are not together. Never undercut her.
sessions.practice: Write one sentence you will not say about their mother this week. If a coparent channel is safe, send one short civil note about the child. If it is not, keep the sentence in your notes.

sessions.title: Sixth Secret: Active Listening

checkpoint.prompt: Active listening means:
choices: Two-way, full attention, not an interrogation

checkpoint.prompt: The usual rival for your attention is:
After they talk, the strong move is to:

sessions.keyline: Two-way. Full attention. Not an interrogation.
sessions.practice: Put the phone face down for one real conversation this week (program peer, coparent, a call you already have). After, write what they actually said, not what you planned to say.

sessions.title: Seventh Secret: Spiritual Equipping

checkpoint.prompt: Spiritual equipping here means:
choices: A required class you sit through
Telling your child what to believe

checkpoint.prompt: What do kids actually watch?
choices: How often you attend a meeting

checkpoint.prompt: Which practice matches this session?
choices: One conviction lived in the open this week
Sign up for a group this week

sessions.keyline: Live convictions a child can trust.
sessions.practice: Name one conviction you will live in the open this week at work, in the program, or at home. Keep your word.

final_qa.prompt: Name one Secret you will practice this week, and the concrete move that proves it.
What did the free assessment show you about where you are strong and where you want to grow?
Who will notice the change first if you keep this practice for thirty days?
What will you do the next time you break a promise you wrote down?
